title: 1991 AHSME Problem 23
statement: If \(ABCD\) is a \(2\times2\) square, \(E\) is the midpoint of \(AB,\) \(F\) is the midpoint of \(BC,\) \(AF\) and \(DE\) intersect at \(I,\) and \(BD\) and \(AF\) intersect at \(H,\) then the area of quadrilateral \(BEIH\) is

solutions.text:
Set \(B=(0,0),\) \(C=(2,0),\) \(D=(2,2),\) and \(A=(0,2).\) Then \(E=(0,1),\) \(F=(1,0),\) and the line intersections are \[ \begin{aligned} I&=AF\cap DE =\left(\frac25,\frac65\right),\\ H&=AF\cap BD =\left(\frac23,\frac23\right). \end{aligned} \] The shoelace formula gives \[ \begin{aligned} [BEIH] &=\frac12\left| \frac4{15}-\frac25-\frac45 \right|\\ &=\frac7{15}. \end{aligned} \]

Thus the correct answer is C.
hints: Assign coordinates to the square and write equations for \(AF,\) \(DE,\) and \(BD\)
Find \(I\) and \(H,\) then use the shoelace formula on \(B,E,I,H\)
